name: Yu Bin
current_role: Founder, Guangzhou Tianyu (Skyfame) real estate group; stepped down as chairman of HK-listed Skyfame Realty (Holdings) (0059.HK) in Feb 2025
profile: Guangzhou property developer (romanised Yu Pan / Yu Bin, 余斌 in HKEX filings) who founded Guangzhou Tianyu Real Estate Development and controlled Hong Kong-listed Skyfame Realty (天譽置業), a developer of residential and commercial projects in Guangzhou and Guangxi. He resigned as Skyfame chairman in February 2025.
interesting_fact: Skyfame's 2006 annual report described him as the founder of 'the prestigious real estate company' Guangzhou Tianyu Real Estate Development Co. – the 'Tianyu' brand in his Forbes listing is the Chinese name (天譽) of Skyfame.
notes: Identity likely (Tianyu = Skyfame's Chinese name; HKEX filings spell him 'Yu Pan') but not fully confirmed. Jan 2026: HKEX issued a director-unsuitability statement/censure against him for not responding to SFC/exchange inquiries (https://www.itiger.com/news/1162125303). Low-profile; poor fit for outreach. No published personal contacts found.

name: Vidya Rashesh Shah
current_role: Executive Chairperson, EdelGive Foundation; Non-Executive Director, Edelweiss Financial Services
profile: Co-founding figure of India's Edelweiss financial group, where she was earlier CFO, after 11 years in investment banking (ICICI, Peregrine, NM Rothschild). In 2008 she founded EdelGive Foundation, Edelweiss's philanthropy arm, which she ran as CEO until 2021 and now chairs, building collaboratives in education, women's empowerment, climate and migration.
interesting_fact: EdelGive pioneered a 'zero-cost platform' model: besides its own grants it channels funding from other institutional and corporate donors to small and mid-sized NGOs without taking a fee.
deep_cut_fact: An IIM-Ahmedabad MBA, she spent her first 11 years in investment banking at ICICI, Peregrine and NM Rothschild before moving into philanthropy; she also sits on boards including Agastya International Foundation, Janaagraha and Mann Deshi Foundation.
notes: Best route is via EdelGive Foundation. A third-party directory lists edelgive@edelweissfin.com (https://philanthropywomen.org/philanthropy-women-funder-database/edelgive-foundation/) but it is not confirmed on EdelGive's own site. Since April 2021 Naghma Mulla is EdelGive CEO.

name: Rakesh Wadhawan
current_role: Promoter and suspended director of Housing Development and Infrastructure Ltd (HDIL), which is in insolvency
profile: Mumbai real-estate promoter who built HDIL into one of Mumbai's largest developers, known for slum-rehabilitation and redevelopment projects, including near Mumbai airport. HDIL entered insolvency in 2019 and its assets are being sold through the NCLT process; he remains involved in disputes over the resolution.
interesting_fact: HDIL's slum-rehabilitation project around Mumbai airport was one of the largest such schemes in India and became central to the company's later financial strain.
notes: Not a suitable outreach target: arrested in 2019 in the PMC Bank case and facing ongoing criminal/insolvency proceedings (e.g. https://www.freepressjournal.in/amp/mumbai/hdil-promoter-rakesh-wadhawan-moves-eow-alleges-illegal-assignment-of-600-crore-yes-bank-loan-to-suraksha-arc). Wealth likely largely wiped out. No published contacts.

name: Michael Pompeo
current_role: Director, VEON Ltd. (since May 2024) and Kyivstar board member; founder, Pompeo Foundation; former US Secretary of State
profile: West Point graduate and Harvard Law alumnus who built and sold Wichita aerospace-parts maker Thayer Aerospace, ran oilfield-equipment firm Sentry International, then served as Kansas congressman, CIA director (2017-18) and US Secretary of State (2018-21). He now sits on the boards of VEON and its Ukrainian unit Kyivstar and runs the Pompeo Foundation.
interesting_fact: He graduated first in his class at West Point in 1986, majoring in engineering management.
deep_cut_fact: In 1996 he and West Point classmates bought three Wichita aircraft-parts shops and a St. Louis tool-and-die firm and named the company Thayer Aerospace after Sylvanus Thayer, the 'father of West Point'; he later ran Sentry International, an oilfield equipment manufacturer – relevant energy-industry roots.
notes: High-profile political figure; likely routed through a speakers bureau or his foundation. Kyivstar board role was framed as safeguarding US investors in Ukraine's largest mobile operator.

name: Aaron Rosenberg
current_role: Chief Financial Officer, BeOne Medicines Ltd. (formerly BeiGene; Nasdaq: ONC) since July 2024
profile: Pharma finance executive who spent more than two decades at Merck, rising to Senior Vice President and Corporate Treasurer, before becoming CFO of oncology company BeiGene (renamed BeOne Medicines after redomiciling to Switzerland in 2025) in July 2024.
interesting_fact: He joined BeiGene just ahead of its transformation into BeOne Medicines, a Swiss-domiciled global oncology company known for the blood-cancer drug Brukinsa.
deep_cut_fact: He joined Merck in 2003 and, before becoming corporate treasurer, ran finance for Merck Animal Health (2015-18) and led Merck's corporate strategy and planning (2018-21). University of Florida finance BS, NYU Stern MBA.
notes: Corporate executive rather than founder; best route is BeOne investor relations.

name: Sumeet Kumar
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Technology Officer, Micromax group; director of MiPhi Semiconductors, Micromax Biofuels, YU Televentures and Bhagwati Products
profile: One of four co-founders (with Rahul Sharma, Rajesh Agarwal and Vikas Jain) who started Micromax in 2000 as an embedded-systems startup and grew it into India's largest home-grown phone brand. The group has since diversified into electronics manufacturing (Bhagwati Products), enterprise SSDs (MiPhi, a JV with Taiwan's Phison), solar modules (Startup Energy) and ethanol (Micromax Biofuels).
interesting_fact: MiPhi Semiconductors, the Micromax-Phison JV (55/45) on whose board he sits, became the first Indian brand to design and manufacture enterprise SSDs aimed at data centres and AI workloads.
deep_cut_fact: Besides chips, he is a director of Micromax Biofuels, which runs a 100 KLPD ethanol plant in Bihar supplying fuel-grade ethanol under India's Ethanol Blending Programme; the group also makes solar modules via Startup Energy.

public_contacts.value: https://micromaxinfo.com/micromax-biofuels (group 'Contact the group' form on site pages)

notes: Sometimes listed as Sumeet Kumar Arora. Strong energy/data-center angle (MiPhi SSDs, solar, ethanol). Low public profile; co-founder Rahul Sharma is the usual spokesperson. Studied B.Tech mechanical engineering at Jamia Millia Islamia per a Naukri company profile (https://companies.naukri.com/micromax-jobs/executive-team).

name: Prashant Godha
current_role: Executive Director, Ipca Laboratories Ltd (since August 2011)
profile: Member of the Godha family that controls Mumbai-based drugmaker Ipca Laboratories, a major producer of APIs and formulations (notably anti-malarials and pain management). A commerce graduate with a PGDBM, he has worked in pharma marketing and general management and has been an Ipca executive director since 2011.
interesting_fact: Ipca's turnaround began in 1975 when his father, chartered accountant Premchand Godha (then managing Amitabh Bachchan's finances), and the Bachchan family acquired the struggling company; the Bachchans exited in 1999 and Ipca is now worth roughly Rs 28,000 crore.
deep_cut_fact: Before joining Ipca's board he spent 12 years (May 1999 - Aug 2011) as wholetime/executive director of Makers Laboratories, a smaller listed pharma company later linked to the Ipca group.
notes: Low public profile; Executive Chairman Premchand Godha and MD & CEO Pranay Godha are the public faces of Ipca. Also non-executive director at Lyka Labs and Resonance Specialties per MarketScreener.

name: Zachary Bradford
current_role: CEO and President, CleanSpark, Inc. (Nasdaq: CLSK) since October 2019
profile: Nevada CPA who joined CleanSpark as CFO in 2014 and became CEO in 2019, steering it from a microgrid/energy-software company into one of the largest US bitcoin miners. In 2026 CleanSpark is repositioning its power and land portfolio (e.g. its Sandersville, Georgia site) for AI/HPC data-center development.
interesting_fact: CleanSpark now pitches its bitcoin-mining sites and power capacity as AI/HPC data-center campuses – a September 2026 investor presentation focused on its Sandersville, GA site – squarely in the podcast's energy/data-center theme.
deep_cut_fact: Before CleanSpark he founded his own public accounting and consulting firm in Henderson, Nevada in June 2013 (still a non-active partner); he earned a bachelor's in accounting and a master of accountancy from Southern Utah University and sits on the board of the Digital Energy Council.
notes: Excellent fit for an energy/data-center podcast; frequent conference speaker (e.g. Bitcoin 2023). Route via pr@cleanspark.com.

name: Wilmot H Kidd
current_role: Chairman of the Board, Central Securities Corporation (NYSE American: CET)
profile: Long-time steward of Central Securities, a New York closed-end investment company: director since 1972, President 1973-2018, CEO 2018-21 and now Chairman (age 84 per the 2026 proxy). He owns about 7% of the fund directly, with a further ~32.5% held by The Endeavor Foundation, giving the Kidd circle effective control of a ~$2bn concentrated, long-horizon portfolio.
interesting_fact: Central Securities' largest holding is a private stake in insurer The Plymouth Rock Company, first bought in 1982 at a cost of $0.7m and valued at about $503m (25.6% of net assets) at 30 Sept 2026.
deep_cut_fact: He has served as a Central Securities director continuously since 1972 – over five decades – and was its President for 45 years (1973-2018); the fund still holds positions it first bought decades ago, e.g. Analog Devices since 1987 and Motorola Solutions since 2000.

public_contacts.value: Corporate office: Central Securities Corporation, 630 Fifth Avenue, New York, NY 10111 (shareholder reports state 'Stockholders' inquiries are welcome')

notes: Very private, old-school value investor; no social media. Best route is a letter to Central Securities' corporate office (business address). John C. Hill is now CEO/President. No published email found (company site blocked automated access).

name: Martin Roper
current_role: Chief Executive Officer, The Vita Coco Company (Nasdaq: COCO); Chairman, MGP Ingredients
profile: Cambridge-trained engineer and Harvard MBA who spent 24 years at Boston Beer (Samuel Adams), as COO and then CEO from 2001-2018, building out Twisted Tea, Angry Orchard and Truly Hard Seltzer. He joined Vita Coco as President in 2019 and has been CEO since May 2022; in 2026 Vita Coco bought premium coconut-water brand Copra.
interesting_fact: During his 17 years as Boston Beer CEO, revenue roughly quadrupled as the company diversified beyond Samuel Adams into Twisted Tea, Angry Orchard and Truly Hard Seltzer.
deep_cut_fact: He holds BA, MA and MEng degrees from Trinity Hall, Cambridge – an engineer by training – and before Vita Coco sat for years on the board of the maker of Power Crunch energy bars (2019-25); since May 2025 he also chairs whiskey/spirits supplier MGP Ingredients.
notes: Consumer-beverage operator; entrepreneurship angle via scaling Boston Beer and Vita Coco. Co-founder Michael Kirban is Executive Chairman. Route via investor relations.

name: Nicolas Papadopoulo
current_role: Chief Executive Officer and Director, Arch Capital Group Ltd. (Nasdaq: ACGL) since October 2024
profile: French-trained actuary and underwriter who joined Arch Re in Bermuda in 2001 and rose through the specialty insurer/reinsurer to run Arch Reinsurance, then its Global Insurance Group, then serve as President and Chief Underwriting Officer before succeeding Marc Grandisson as group CEO in October 2024.
interesting_fact: He has spent his entire 25-year Arch career there since joining Arch Re Bermuda in 2001; in his first full year as CEO (2025), Arch's tangible book value per share grew at a 33.65% annualised rate over 2023-25 and the company bought back $1.9bn of stock.
deep_cut_fact: Before reinsurance, he worked as an insurance examiner at France's Ministry of Finance (Insurance Department); he is a graduate of École Polytechnique and ENSAE (master's in statistics) and a Fellow of the French Actuarial Society.

public_contacts.value: dwatson@archgroup.com (Donald Watson, Investor Relations, as listed on Arch earnings releases)

notes: Bermuda-based insurance CEO; low media profile. Possible energy/data-center angle: Arch underwrites property, energy and construction risks. Route via investor relations.

name: David B. Gendell
current_role: Director, IES Holdings, Inc. (Nasdaq: IESC) since 2012
profile: Investor and operator who spent 2004-2018 at Tontine Associates, the industrials-focused fund that is IES Holdings' majority stockholder, and has sat on the IES board since 2012 (Chairman 2015-16, Vice Chairman 2016-17, interim Director of Operations 2017-19). IES, an electrical and infrastructure contractor, is now booming on data-center demand.
interesting_fact: IES Holdings' backlog hit $4.5bn at June 30, 2026, up 91% in the fiscal year, driven primarily by electrical and custom-engineered work for data centers – it has been training extra crews specifically for the data-center market.
deep_cut_fact: Before Tontine he ran venture-backed startups: President & COO of real-estate data aggregator Homserv (1999-2002) and of practice-management software firm Cogent Design (2002-03). He is Chairman Emeritus of the Board of Advisors of the Duke Global Health Institute.

public_contacts.value: IESC@alpha-ir.com (Alpha IR Group, IES investor relations)

notes: Brother of IES Executive Chairman / Tontine founder Jeffrey Gendell. Strong data-center angle via IES. Low public profile; route via IES IR.

name: Fran Horowitz
current_role: Chief Executive Officer and Director, Abercrombie & Fitch Co. (NYSE: ANF); Director, Jersey Mike's Subs
profile: Retail merchant who spent 13 years at Bloomingdale's plus stints at Express and Ann Taylor LOFT before joining Abercrombie & Fitch in 2014 to run Hollister. CEO since February 2017, she led A&F's turnaround from its exclusionary-era image into one of retail's strongest comebacks; she also sits on the board of Jersey Mike's (Conagra board 2021-25).
interesting_fact: In 2026 the National Retail Federation named her 'The Visionary 2026' for building authentic, customer-centric retail brands.
deep_cut_fact: She started out in buying jobs at Bergdorf Goodman and the long-gone New York department store Bonwit Teller, after a liberal-arts degree from Lafayette College (1985) and a Fordham MBA (1990); she grew up attending high school in Armonk, NY.
notes: Professional CEO rather than founder; turnaround story is a strong podcast hook. Route via A&F public relations. Also on Jersey Mike's board (JMKE).

name: Brian K. McCarthy
current_role: Former President, Global Sales & Field Operations, Rubrik, Inc. (resigned Feb 6, 2026 'to pursue another opportunity'; new role not confirmed)
profile: Enterprise-software sales leader who was Rubrik's Chief Revenue Officer from February 2021, taking the data-security company through its 2024 IPO, and then President of Global Sales and Field Operations until February 2026. Previously CRO of analytics firm ThoughtSpot (2018-21) and VP of Sales at AppDynamics (acquired by Cisco).
interesting_fact: He led Rubrik's go-to-market through its April 2024 NYSE IPO, one of the notable enterprise-software listings of that year, after doing the same scaling job at ThoughtSpot.
deep_cut_fact: Unusually for a software sales chief, he holds a Bachelor of Arts in Theology and History from the Franciscan University of Steubenville.
notes: Left Rubrik in Feb 2026 (8-K: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1943896/000119312526037791/d52441d8k.htm); his new employer could not be confirmed (web search quota exhausted). No published contacts; check LinkedIn for current role. Rubrik PR/IR (IR@rubrik.com) no longer a relevant route.

name: David A Sumoski
current_role: Retired (June 2026) Executive Vice President and former Chief Operating Officer (2021-Jan 2026), Nucor Corporation
profile: Career Nucor steelman who joined as an electrical supervisor at Nucor Steel-Berkeley in 1995 and rose through maintenance and plant leadership (GM of Nucor Steel Marion and Nucor Steel Memphis) to EVP in 2014 and Chief Operating Officer of America's largest steelmaker in 2021. He stepped down as COO in January 2026 and retired in June 2026.
interesting_fact: As COO (2021-Jan 2026) he oversaw operations at Nucor, North America's largest recycler, which makes steel mainly from scrap in electric arc furnaces – about 20 million gross tons of scrap recycled in 2025.
deep_cut_fact: He started at Nucor in 1995 as an electrical supervisor at the Nucor Steel-Berkeley mill in South Carolina, later its maintenance manager, before running the Marion (Ohio) and Memphis mills – a shop-floor-to-COO career.

public_contacts.value: katherine.miller@nucor.com (Nucor media inquiries, as published in Nucor press releases)

notes: Now retired from Nucor; low public profile. Nucor's published media contact is the only route found. Energy angle: EAF steelmaking is highly power-intensive.

name: David M Lowe
current_role: Retired (2026) Chief Financial Officer and Treasurer, Graco Inc. (NYSE: GGG); succeeded by Sanjiv Gupta on April 15, 2026
profile: Graco lifer who joined the Minneapolis fluid-handling equipment maker in 1995 as Treasurer and over three decades ran its Lubrication Equipment division, European operations, Industrial Products and Process divisions before serving as CFO and Treasurer from June 2021. He announced his retirement in February 2026 and stayed in a non-executive role through May 2026.
interesting_fact: He is one of the few CFOs to have run major operating businesses first – heading Graco's European operations (1999-2005) and its Industrial Products and Worldwide Process divisions before taking the finance chief role at age 65.
deep_cut_fact: He joined Graco in 1995 as Treasurer and a year later moved into operations as VP of the Lubrication Equipment Division – then returned to the Treasurer title 25 years later when he became CFO and Treasurer in 2021.
notes: Retired from Graco in 2026 (8-K: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/42888/000119312526085816/d104194d8k.htm). No published personal contacts; Graco media contact (Kirstie_L_Foster@graco.com) is a corporate route only. Low outreach priority.

name: Brendan Horgan
current_role: Chief Executive Officer and Director, Sunbelt Rentals Holdings, Inc. (NYSE: SUNB; formerly Ashtead Group plc)
profile: American equipment-rental executive with nearly 30 years at Sunbelt Rentals/Ashtead: COO of North America from 2003, CEO of North America from 2011, and Ashtead group Chief Executive from 2019. He led the group's redomiciliation from London to a primary NYSE listing as Sunbelt Rentals Holdings, completed in February 2026.
interesting_fact: He steered one of the FTSE 100's biggest companies to move its primary listing from London to New York – the Ashtead-to-Sunbelt reorganisation completed on Feb 27, 2026, keeping only a secondary LSE listing. Sunbelt cites mega projects and energy among its strongest demand drivers.
deep_cut_fact: A Radford University (Virginia) graduate, he has spent essentially his whole career at Sunbelt and has sat on the Ashtead board since January 2011 – eight years before becoming group CEO.
notes: Good fit: equipment rental for mega projects incl. data centers and energy. Route via H/Advisors Abernathy (PR agency).

name: Anre D Williams
current_role: Director, Navan, Inc. (Nasdaq: NAVN) since 2025; Senior Executive Advisor, American Express (Feb 2025 - Nov 2026, per Navan's 2026 proxy)
profile: Veteran American Express executive (joined 1990) who ran Global Merchant & Network Services, then served as Group President, Enterprise Services and CEO of American Express National Bank, responsible for over 60% of AmEx's revenues, and sat on AmEx's Executive Committee 2018-2026. He has since moved into board roles, including travel/expense platform Navan.
interesting_fact: As CEO of American Express National Bank (2021-25) he oversaw the unit responsible for more than 60 percent of American Express's total revenues.
deep_cut_fact: A Stanford economics BA and Wharton MBA who joined American Express in 1990, he served 13 years (2010-23) on the board of Illinois Tool Works and, early in his career, on the board of metals processor Joseph T. Ryerson & Son (2004-07).
notes: Transitioning out of American Express in late 2026; now primarily a board member. No personal published contacts found.

name: Christopher J. Senner
current_role: Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer, Exelixis, Inc. (Nasdaq: EXEL) since July 2015
profile: Biopharma finance executive who spent 18 years at Wyeth (rising to CFO of its U.S. pharmaceuticals and BioPharma units) and five years as VP Corporate Finance at Gilead before becoming CFO of oncology company Exelixis in 2015, during the build-out of its cabozantinib (Cabometyx) franchise, which now drives quarterly revenue of roughly $650m+.
interesting_fact: He has been Exelixis's CFO through its transformation into a profitable commercial oncology company: Q3 2026 total revenues were $658.7 million, led by the cabozantinib franchise.
deep_cut_fact: A Bentley College finance graduate, he spent 18 years at Wyeth before Pfizer's 2009 takeover, and since 2019 has also served on the board of clinical-stage biotech Quince Therapeutics.

public_contacts.value: csenner@exelixis.com (listed by Exelixis as press-release contact)
apeters@exelixis.com (Andrew Peters, SVP Strategy & Investor Relations)

notes: Corporate CFO; his work email is published by Exelixis as the financial contact on earnings releases. Biotech focus – limited fit with energy/data-center theme.
